subject: zoology_2
question_text: Where are the testes located in man? Name the protective coverings of each testis.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.54, VSAQ 101. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Where they lie
steps.why: The scrotum keeps the testes a few degrees below body temperature, which sperm need in order to develop.
common_mistakes: Placing the testes inside the abdomen. They hang outside it.
steps.memory_tip: Outside the abdomen, in the scrotal sacs.
steps.margin_note: One line for the place, one for the coverings.
lines: The testes of man lie in a pouch outside
the abdomen called the scrotal sacs, or

steps.label: The two coverings
steps.why: The inner fibrous coat holds the testis together and the outer peritoneal coat lets it move smoothly inside the scrotum.
common_mistakes: Naming only one covering. Two are asked.
Confusing tunica albuginea with tunica vaginalis.
steps.memory_tip: Albuginea is the white fibrous coat; vaginalis is the outer sheath.
steps.margin_note: Both names carry the second mark.

lines.text: Outside it is a peritoneal tunica vaginalis

insider_note: Two questions, two marks. Name both coverings — tunica albuginea and tunica vaginalis — or half the answer is missing.
